newsitem.title: USA: Many U.S. fund investors would sell at market drop.
newsitem.headline: Many U.S. fund investors would sell at market drop.

text.p: About 40 percent of U.S. mutual fund investors would sell their holdings if the U.S. stock market declined 15 percent, according to a nationwide survey conducted by Smith Barney.
Asked what they would do if the market declined 15 percent, 40 percent said they would "sell everything" or "sell something."
About 53 percent said they would "wait and see" how the market performed, according to the survey.

"The truth is that investor behavior has a far greater impact on investment returns than does mutual fund performance," said Jessica Bibliowicz, who heads Smith Barney Mutual Funds. "Investors often tend to sell their shares when the market declines -- usually the wrong time to sell."
The survey questioned 310 investors by telephone last month. The surbey error rate is plus or minus six percentage points.
Smith Barney is a unit of Travelers Group Inc.
